_comment: 词条释义英文。键 = md 文件名（不含扩展名），必须与 _data/glossary/terms/ 的文件名一字不差。
_fields: purpose / def / why，对应源 md 的同名字段。缺字段时英文态回退中文（可接受降级）。
_progress: 全部译完（116 个有释义的词条逐条人工翻译，六层全覆盖；INDEX.md 无释义不译）

人工智能.purpose: Let machines do what used to need human intelligence — see images, understand speech, write, and decide.
def: A broad field: making machines behave in ways we recognise as intelligent. It is not one technology but many, and today's chatbots are only a branch of it.
人工智能.why: People often use "AI" to mean a chat model. Strictly speaking a large language model is one approach inside AI, not AI itself — most claims about "AI" are really claims about one kind of model.

机器学习.purpose: Instead of writing rules by hand, let the machine find patterns in data.
def: A method where a system improves at a task by fitting parameters to examples, rather than following rules a programmer wrote.
机器学习.why: It is the foundation under essentially everything called AI today. Knowing where the rules came from tells you what the system can and cannot do.

深度学习.purpose: Stack many layers so the network learns its own features instead of being told them.
def: Machine learning using multi-layer neural networks, where representations are learned from raw data rather than hand-designed.
深度学习.why: It is what made image, speech and language tasks leap forward. Understanding it helps you judge which claims about "deep learning" are real.

神经网络.purpose: A network of simple units whose combined output can approximate very complex functions.
def: Layers of connected units, each applying a small transformation, whose overall behaviour is learned from data rather than specified.
神经网络.why: It is the mechanism behind deep learning. You do not need the maths to use it, but it explains both what it can do and why it fails in particular ways.

训练.purpose: Let the system learn its parameters from data by repeated exposure.
def: Fitting parameters so predictions match targets, usually by minimising a loss over many examples.
训练.why: Training determines what the model knows. It is also where cost and bias enter — training data is not neutral.

推理.purpose: The model you trained is now answering real queries — a different phase with different costs.
def: Running a trained model to produce an answer. Often confused with "reasoning", but inference simply means using the model.
推理.why: Training and inference have different cost structures. It explains why a model can be cheap to make and expensive to serve.

参数.purpose: The numbers the training process adjusts; everything the model knows lives in them.
def: Weights and biases inside the network. Model size usually refers to how many there are, and larger counts generally mean more capacity.
参数.why: It grounds abstract claims: a "7B model" is a statement about parameter count, not about being better than everything else.

提示词.purpose: The instructions you give the model, and often the main lever you actually control.
def: The input text shaping the model's behaviour. In a chat interface it is what you type; in an API it is part of the request.
提示词.why: For using models, prompt quality often matters more than model choice — the same model behaves very differently under different phrasing.

上下文窗口.purpose: How much the model can see at once — the page of text it can keep in mind while answering.
def: The token budget for one request: system prompt, documents, conversation history and the reply all draw from it.
上下文窗口.why: It sets a hard ceiling on what can be asked. "It forgot what I told it" is usually a context-window limit, not a memory bug.

幻觉.purpose: The model states something plausible and confident that is simply not true.
def: Output that is fluent and confident but factually wrong. It comes from producing likely-sounding text rather than retrieving verified facts.
幻觉.why: It is the single biggest practical risk with language models, and the reason fact-checking matters more than ever.

多模态.purpose: Handle text, images, audio and video in one system rather than bolting separate models together.
def: A model that takes or produces more than one kind of input or output, so images and text can be reasoned about together.
多模态.why: It is what makes document Q&A, screenshot understanding and video generation practical rather than staged pipelines.

工具调用.purpose: Let the model actually do things — search, run code, edit files — rather than only describe them.
def: A mechanism where the model emits a structured request for a function, the system runs it, and the result goes back into the conversation.
工具调用.why: It is what turns a language model into a usable assistant. It also introduces real risk: the model can act wrongly, not just speak wrongly.

微调.purpose: Teach an existing model a specific task or style, rather than describing the task in the prompt.
def: Further training of an already-trained model on task-specific data, changing its weights rather than its instructions.
微调.why: It can beat prompting for a narrow task, but it costs more and is harder to maintain. Prompting first is usually the right order.

大模型 - 大语言模型.purpose: After training, the learned parameters that let a system generalise to inputs it has never seen.
def: The trained artefact: parameters plus the architecture that produced them. "Loading a model" means loading these, not running a program.
大模型 - 大语言模型.why: Model and product are different things. Many misunderstandings about AI products come from treating a model as if it were an application.

智能体 - Agent.purpose: Stop answering and start acting: let the model take multi-step actions on its own.
def: A system where a model plans, calls tools, reads results and repeats until the task is done, rather than replying once.
智能体 - Agent.why: It is the difference between "it tells you how" and "it does it for you". Most of the practical value in agents comes from tool use, not conversation.

向量 - 嵌入.purpose: Represent text as coordinates, so meaning can be compared by geometry rather than by string match.
def: Turning text into a list of numbers where closer vectors mean closer meaning. It is how semantic search and retrieval work.
向量 - 嵌入.why: Most retrieval systems are built on it. It also explains why keyword search still matters alongside vector search.

联网 - 检索增强.purpose: Let the model look things up before answering, instead of answering from memory alone.
def: Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch relevant passages first, then have the model answer using them, ideally with citations.
联网 - 检索增强.why: It is the most practical way to reduce hallucination and give a model private or current knowledge.

_removed: 「通用人工智能」与「蒸馏」无对应源文件，已移除 —— 键名对不上会被构建器静默忽略，留着只会让人误以为已覆盖。

AI 搜索.purpose: Describe what you want in a sentence instead of keywords, and get an answer directly.
def: Search products that understand natural-language queries and generate an answer instead of returning links.
AI 搜索.why: It changes how you look things up, and partly replaces conventional search engines.

AI 芯片.purpose: Chips built specifically for AI computation — more efficient than general GPUs, but with a more closed ecosystem.
def: Processors optimised for matrix computation, usually referring to AI-specific accelerator hardware of various kinds.
AI 芯片.why: It determines how large a model you can fit onto a device at a given price.

CLIP.purpose: Lets a model relate text descriptions to image content — the foundation of text-to-image generation.
def: Maps images and text into the same space, so the phrase "a cat" lands near the visual features of cats.
CLIP.why: Nearly every text-to-image tool ships it. It sets the ceiling on how well a model understands a prompt.

ControlNet.purpose: Gives precise control over the result using line art, depth maps or pose skeletons.
def: A control network attached to a diffusion model, constraining the shape and pose of what gets generated.
ControlNet.why: The most practical control mechanism in image generation, and essential when you need an exact composition.

偏好对齐.purpose: Makes a model's output match human preference, rather than merely continuing text.
def: Training a model on human rankings of several candidate answers so it tends to be helpful, harmless and honest.
偏好对齐.why: It explains why a model sometimes refuses or is excessively agreeable — that is trained behaviour, not a technical limit.

具身智能.purpose: Giving AI a body so it can sense its surroundings and act — the robotics side of things.
def: A technology system extending AI into the physical world, covering perception, control and planning.
具身智能.why: It is the branch of AI furthest from everyday life, and also the largest category in this directory (87 entries).

分块.purpose: Cut a long document into pieces before feeding it to the model. How you chunk decides how accurate the answer is.
def: The step in a RAG pipeline that splits a document into passages. Too small loses context; too large does not fit the context window.
分块.why: The most overlooked yet most consequential step in RAG. Many "the AI answered wrongly" cases trace back to bad chunking.

向量数据库.purpose: A database built to store and search those numeric arrays, so RAG can find the relevant passages among millions of documents in an instant.
def: Storage engines designed for similarity search — a query traditional databases cannot serve.
向量数据库.why: If you are building RAG this is a must-have. Understanding it tells you why an approach is fast or slow.

扩散模型.purpose: The dominant method for image generation: "wipe" an image out of noise step by step.
def: A generative model that starts from random noise and produces an image through many denoising steps.
Almost every image-generation tool today, including the open-source Stable Diffusion family, is built on it.
扩散模型.why: It is the technical base of image generation. Understanding it explains why generation takes a moment and why "steps" is a parameter.

推理模型.purpose: Works through a chain of internal steps before answering, which markedly improves accuracy on hard problems.
def: A model that produces intermediate reasoning before its conclusion — typically one with a thinking or reasoning mode.
The cost is slower responses and more output tokens.
推理模型.why: The single most important attribute when choosing a model: reasoning models for coding, arithmetic and planning; ordinary models for speed and cost.

数字人.purpose: A virtual person with an appearance and a voice, used for customer service, virtual presenters and similar.
def: A virtual human form combining speech synthesis, image generation and animation.
数字人.why: It is a combined application of multimodal capability, and a category of its own in this directory.

机器视觉.purpose: Lets a camera "see" — recognise people, objects, text and actions.
def: Technology that extracts and understands information from images and video.
机器视觉.why: The technical foundation of autonomous driving, security and medical imaging — two stages along the same direction as multimodal models.

温度.purpose: Controls how random the output is. Lower is steadier; higher is more creative.
def: A sampling parameter controlling how often the highest-probability token is chosen. A temperature of 0 gives the most deterministic output.
温度.why: Low temperature for code and extraction; high temperature for naming and copywriting. It is one of the few parameters you can adjust directly.

潜空间.purpose: The key mechanism in image generation — the model works in a compressed space, not on raw pixels.
def: An encoder first compresses an image into a lower-dimensional space; generation happens there and a decoder restores it.
潜空间.why: It explains why image models need to load a VAE, and why that compression affects fine detail.

知识截止.purpose: The date boundary of a model's training data. Anything after it, the model does not know.
def: The cut-off date of the training corpus. Information later than that was never learned.
知识截止.why: Ask it about recent events, today's news or current prices and it either does not know or makes something up. Anything current needs search.

ACP.purpose: Let AI coding tools from different vendors plug into the same editor.
def: A protocol agreement that lets an editor load agent implementations from any vendor.
ACP.why: It is the same idea as MCP — a standard interface instead of per-vendor integration.

App Server.purpose: Let one AI session hand off between terminal, editor and web.
def: A design where AI session state lives in a standalone service that several front ends can attach to.
App Server.why: It explains why some tools let you close the terminal and carry on in another interface: the session lives in a service, not in the terminal.

MCP.purpose: A standard interface for connecting AI to external tools and data in one uniform way, without a bespoke integration per service.
def: An open protocol proposed by Anthropic describing, in one specification, which tools an AI may call and which resources it may read.
It plays the role of USB-C for AI: whatever device you plug in, the interface is the same.
MCP.why: If you want to connect data to an AI, this is the least-effort and most general approach today. This site's MCP track covers it.

人机协作.purpose: A human confirms the key steps instead of the system running on unattended.
def: Inserting human review at specific points in a flow, so a person decides whether to continue or how to change it.
人机协作.why: Anything that writes files, sends requests, spends money or modifies a database should have a human checkpoint. This is the main lever against accidents.

仓库级理解.purpose: Let the AI read the whole project, not just the file that happens to be open.
def: The AI builds an index and structural model of the entire codebase, so it can answer across files and reason about blast radius.
仓库级理解.why: This is the dividing line between Copilot-class tools and simple completion. Refactoring tasks require it.

代码补全.purpose: Complete the following code automatically in the editor, based on context.
def: Inferring and inserting the code that follows, from the cursor position and what is already written.
代码补全.why: The earliest and most basic AI coding capability — every IDE-class tool started here.

参考服务器.purpose: Official "reference" implementations showing how the protocol should be written.
def: Minimal implementations published by the MCP project — not for end users, but for developers to reference and test against.
参考服务器.why: Reading the official implementation is the fastest way to understand a protocol — far quicker than the documentation.

可观测性.purpose: See what the model actually did this run, what it cost, and which step went wrong.
def: Recording the call chain, each step's input and output, token usage and latency so problems can be traced.
可观测性.why: Model behaviour is probabilistic; without records you can never diagnose a problem. This is what separates a demo from a production system.

多 Agent 协作.purpose: Split a complex job across several roles, each strong at something different.
def: Multiple agents with different tools and prompts working together — the classic pattern is planner plus executor plus reviewer.
The cost is that token consumption and latency both multiply.
多 Agent 协作.why: Not everything needs multiple agents. On simple tasks one agent with tools is faster and more reliable.

工作流编排.purpose: Fix a repeated pattern: the AI does a step, a human confirms, the next step runs.
def: Writing the step order and branch conditions explicitly in code, rather than leaving every decision to the model.
工作流编排.why: Reliable production systems are mostly human-in-the-loop workflows, not fully autonomous agents. This is the key design decision for controlling risk.

差异对比.purpose: See exactly what the AI changed — the most important step when accepting AI-written code.
def: Comparing before and after line by line, the basic means of reviewing AI output.
差异对比.why: A pattern that recurs in official guidance: keep AI changes under version control, diffable and revertible. That is a precondition for safety.

技能 - Skills.purpose: Package a repetitive workflow into a reusable capability.
def: Wrapping a set of prompts, tool configuration and execution steps so they can be called across many tasks.
技能 - Skills.why: It is the mechanism that moves you from re-explaining every time to configuring once and reusing.

护栏.purpose: Constrain what the model may and may not do, so it does not drift or take dangerous actions.
def: A layer of checks on the input and output side — keywords, permissions, or another model's judgement.
护栏.why: If you give an agent the ability to write files and run commands, you must give it guardrails. This is a direct trade of capability for risk.

持续集成.purpose: Tests and checks run automatically as soon as code is committed.
def: An automated verification pipeline that triggers a build and tests on commit.
持续集成.why: It decides whether AI output can be verified automatically — and verifiable output is what makes batch use safe.

提示注入.purpose: The main security risk in agent systems: content that talks the model into doing something you did not intend.
def: An attack where instructions hidden in retrieved documents, tool output or a web page hijack the model's behaviour.
提示注入.why: It is the single most important thing to understand before deploying an agent that reads untrusted content.

版本控制.purpose: Record every change and roll back at will — the safety foundation of AI-assisted coding.
def: A mechanism tracking the history of file changes, supporting collaboration and rollback.
版本控制.why: AI makes mistakes and deletes the wrong file. Without version control you cannot afford to let it act.

终端 Agent.purpose: Run tasks autonomously in the command line: edit files, run tests, commit code.
def: An AI agent running in the terminal, able to operate the development environment directly.
终端 Agent.why: It suits automation and scripting better than IDE-class tools, and is the only option in scripted or CI environments.

结构化输出.purpose: Make the model's answer a strict format (JSON and the like) rather than a paragraph of prose.
def: Constraining the model to output machine-parsable structure that a program can consume directly.
结构化输出.why: A precondition for tool calling. Without it a model cannot reliably tell a program what to call or which arguments to pass.

记忆.purpose: Let an agent remember things across conversations instead of restating the background every time.
def: Persisting historical information so later sessions can retrieve it.
Two approaches: store it in the program (controllable), or in external storage the model can reach (flexible, but then permissions matter).
记忆.why: "The AI forgets everything every time" is the most common complaint in use, and the answer is a memory layer.

评估.purpose: Decide whether an approach is actually good, rather than merely plausible-sounding.
def: A fixed set of questions plus scoring criteria, to compare models, prompts or approaches quantitatively.
评估.why: Without evaluation there is no basis for improvement. It is the dividing line between a product built seriously and one that merely sounds good.

远程执行.purpose: A cloud agent runs tasks on your machine, so closing the laptop does not stop it.
def: Moving execution to a remote server, with the local machine acting only as a viewer.
远程执行.why: It is the basis for long-running tasks and the core difference between hosted and self-hosted setups.

配对编程.purpose: AI as a programming partner taking part in development in real time.
def: The practice of two people writing code together, extended to a human plus AI collaboration model.
配对编程.why: It is the original concept behind every AI coding tool — they all automate this pattern to different degrees.

长时任务.purpose: Work running for hours or days across many contexts.
def: Tasks exceeding a single context window or session, requiring external progress storage and staged resumption.
长时任务.why: This is the ceiling on agent capability. For a framework claiming long-running tasks, check how it stores progress.

KV 缓存.purpose: Stops the model recomputing the whole passage on every token it generates — this is what makes generation speed usable.
def: Caching the attention intermediates already computed, so only new tokens need incremental work.
The cost is that it **occupies VRAM continuously** — which directly caps how long a context you can afford.
KV 缓存.why: It is the most common cause of OOM when deploying locally. Raise the context size and you hit this first.

Transformer.purpose: The architecture underneath every mainstream large model today.
def: A neural network structure built around the attention mechanism, handling the relationships across a whole passage of text.
It processes a sentence in parallel rather than one word at a time — which is why it scales to trillions of parameters.
Transformer.why: It is the root of large models. Understand it and the origin of context windows, hallucination and the KV cache becomes clear.

上下文窗口的代价.purpose: A larger context window is slower and more expensive — it is not free capacity.
def: A bigger window means attention computation and KV cache memory both grow.
上下文窗口的代价.why: It explains a counter-intuitive result: pasting in everything at once is often worse than retrieving in batches with RAG.

传输方式.purpose: How your data actually reaches the model or tool: staying on your machine, or going to a third party.
def: The channel data moves through between components. In-process local transfer and cross-network transfer have very different safety properties.
The two common forms: local inter-process communication, and remote HTTP requests.
传输方式.why: It is the first question to ask when deciding whether your data can leak. **Anything sent to a remote service is inherently unsuitable for sensitive material.**

位置编码.purpose: Lets the model know the order of words in a sentence.
def: Attaching a set of numbers to each position so the model can tell "the cat chased the dog" from "the dog chased the cat".
位置编码.why: It explains why comprehension of long passages degrades noticeably once you exceed the context window.

嵌入层.purpose: The first step of turning words into numeric vectors — models only work in numbers internally.
def: The layer mapping each token to a high-dimensional vector inside the model — the origin of vector retrieval.
嵌入层.why: It connects the conceptual layer to the applied one: the embedding you use in practice is this.

推理成本.purpose: What a model costs per answer, determined by how many tokens go in and come out.
def: Usually priced separately for input and output tokens, with output more expensive.
The same model can cost an order of magnitude more depending on how you phrase the question.
推理成本.why: The easiest trap to fall into when using AI day to day, and a cost item any model choice has to account for.

注意力机制.purpose: When processing one word, the model automatically looks at the most relevant other words in the sentence.
def: Computing how related each word is to every other word, and aggregating information weighted by that.
"Attention" inside a Transformer and "the model isn't paying attention" in everyday speech are the same word meaning different things.
注意力机制.why: It explains why models can resolve references across a long sentence — and is one technical root of the context length limit.

训练算力.purpose: Both training and inference burn compute. This is AI's hardest resource threshold.
def: Training needs many GPUs and a lot of time; inference is far cheaper but costs continuously.
训练算力.why: It explains why large-model companies burn money, and why running one locally means doing the VRAM arithmetic first.

预训练.purpose: Predicting the next token over vast text — the stage where a model absorbs world knowledge.
def: The first training run, with a single objective: continue the text. It costs hundreds of millions.
预训练.why: It explains why a model "knows a bit about everything": that is the result of reading widely, not learning for your task.

bpw.purpose: The numeric form of a quantisation level: how many bits each weight averages.
def: A measure of how aggressively a model is quantised. This site groups them into five tiers: extreme compression, long context first, balanced, conservative and near-lossless.
Lower numbers mean a smaller model.
bpw.why: It unifies vendor-specific names like Q4, Q8 and Q3 into one comparable number — the most practical yardstick when choosing.

GGUF.purpose: The de facto standard file format for running models locally. The llama.cpp ecosystem accepts little else.
def: The model file format defined by the llama.cpp project, packaging the model structure together with its quantisation parameters.
The vast majority of community quantisations ship in this format.
GGUF.why: If you run models locally, this is what you download. Other formats usually need an extra conversion step.

GPU 层卸载.purpose: Give part of the model to the GPU and keep the rest on the CPU — the compromise when VRAM falls short.
def: Assigning layers across devices: whatever fits in VRAM goes to the GPU, the rest runs on the CPU backed by system memory.
In llama.cpp this is usually controlled with the `-ngl` flag.
GPU 层卸载.why: It lets models that "almost" fit run at all, at a clear cost in speed. A trade-off, not a free lunch.

GPU.purpose: The chip that actually does the matrix arithmetic. Large models run on it; a CPU is far too slow.
def: A processor built for large-scale parallel computation, originally designed for graphics rendering and now the workhorse of model training and inference.
GPU.why: It decides whether a model runs and how fast. On the same card, VRAM capacity matters more than the compute tier.

llama.cpp.purpose: The mainstream open-source engine for running large models on an ordinary computer, CPU included.
def: An inference engine written in C/C++ that emphasises lightness and cross-platform support, with mixed CPU and GPU inference.
It is the foundation of the local deployment ecosystem — many quantisations exist specifically for it.
llama.cpp.why: The default choice for local deployment. Picking it means access to the largest set of quantisations and community support.

Prompt Cache.purpose: Cache repeated system prompts and documents, saving time and money when asking about the same context again.
def: Reusing processing already done for an identical prefix so it is not computed twice.
Prompt Cache.why: System prompts in agent work are usually long, so caching meaningfully lowers cost. It is also why this site does not host models itself.

vLLM.purpose: A serving engine for running models at high concurrency on a server.
def: A production-oriented high-throughput inference engine that improves concurrency via techniques such as continuous batching.
vLLM.why: You will not need it for a personal local setup, but you do need something like it to offer an API to others.

专家卸载.purpose: For sparse models with many experts where only a few activate per token, keep the rarely-used experts in memory.
def: A mixture-of-experts (MoE) model activates only a few experts per inference, so the remaining weights can sit on slower storage and be fetched as needed.
专家卸载.why: It explains why some very large models run on a single card: not all weights participate at once.

吞吐.purpose: How many tokens per second come out. It determines how long you wait for a long generation.
def: Tokens produced per second. Higher throughput means faster long-form generation.
吞吐.why: It is a separate metric from time-to-first-token, and the two must be read together — looking at only one misleads the actual experience.

张量并行.purpose: Split one model across several GPUs when it does not fit on a single card.
def: Partitioning model weights across multiple GPUs by dimension, each computing part, with inter-card communication required.
张量并行.why: The main technique for multi-GPU deployment. Prefer a single card when VRAM allows — communication overhead slows things down.

显存.purpose: Memory on the graphics card. If the model does not fit, it simply does not run — nothing else matters.
def: High-speed memory on the GPU. Model weights and the KV cache both live there, and overflowing means it cannot run.
VRAM is the first hard threshold for local deployment — not a performance question but a can-it-run-at-all question.
显存.why: It is the only budget you must settle before running a model locally. Choosing a quantisation tier is essentially about fitting inside VRAM.

API - 接口调用.purpose: Do not run a model yourself — pay per use for someone else's.
def: Send the prompt to a model provider over a network interface and get the result back.
API - 接口调用.why: This is how most people actually use AI. No graphics card needed and you pay as you go; the cost is that data leaves your machine and the bill keeps going.

供应商锁定.purpose: The deeper you go, the harder it is to switch models or providers.
def: Depending on a vendor's proprietary prompt formats, tool-calling conventions or fine-tuning formats, so migrating costs a lot.
供应商锁定.why: The long-term cost most easily missed during selection. The test: how much code changes if you swap models?

单次调用成本.purpose: What a task actually costs to run, not just the unit price.
def: Unit price times the tokens actually consumed. Consumption can differ by orders of magnitude between tasks.
单次调用成本.why: Choosing a model on unit price alone is easy to get wrong. Two models can cost the same per token and end up in the opposite order overall.

可替换性.purpose: How much has to change if you swap models or providers.
def: How dependent a design is on a particular provider. Open protocols and formats raise substitutability substantially.
可替换性.why: The most easily overlooked item in long-term cost, and the basis of resilience when something breaks.

基准测试.purpose: Compare models head to head using a shared question set.
def: Scores from standardised evaluation suites such as MMLU or HumanEval.
基准测试.why: Important but not to be trusted blindly — public leaderboards go stale and may have little relation to your actual task.

开源模型.purpose: The weights are public: you can download them, run them on your own machine, and pay nobody.
def: Models whose parameter weights are published. Note that open code and open weights are different things — only open weights mean you can self-host.
开源模型.why: It decides whether you can work offline, whether you can fine-tune, and whether private data has to leave.

总分 - 综合评测.purpose: Collapse several benchmark scores into one number for quick comparison.
def: A weighted aggregate across several evaluation dimensions. Weighting differs substantially between providers.
总分 - 综合评测.why: When you see "an overall score of X", ask first: how was it weighted, which question set, and when was the data collected.

数据不出网.purpose: Your material never passes through a third party. This is a hard requirement in many situations.
def: All data processed on machines you control, never uploaded to an external service.
数据不出网.why: Where contracts, personal data or source code are involved, this is the line between usable and not — not a nice-to-have.

服务中断风险.purpose: Depending on someone else's service means it may raise prices, shut down, or rate-limit you.
def: The risk that an unavailable third-party service blocks your work.
服务中断风险.why: If a critical process depends entirely on one provider, this is a very real operational risk.

自托管成本.purpose: Running locally costs no per-token fee, but hardware, electricity and operations are real costs.
def: The total of hardware purchase, power, VRAM expansion and the ongoing maintenance work.
自托管成本.why: It makes the common assumption "local is always cheaper than an API" testable — compute it against your actual usage.

许可证.purpose: What you may do with it: use, modify, or commercialise. The constraint most often overlooked during selection.
def: The licence terms attached to a model; providers vary widely in strictness.
The points to check: commercial use allowed? Redistribution allowed? Do derivatives inherit the original licence?
许可证.why: A hard legal constraint. However good the technology is, if the licence forbids it, you cannot use it.

路由.purpose: Send easy questions to a cheap fast model and hard ones to a strong model.
def: Mechanism that picks a model automatically based on task complexity.
路由.why: The most effective way to control cost and quality together, and standard practice in current product design.

迭代速度.purpose: How fast the project moves and how stable its versions are.
def: Release frequency and stability. Frequent updates mean faster improvement but also possible breaking changes.
迭代速度.why: It decides whether you are chasing something moving quickly or using a tool that is settling down.

退出成本.purpose: What it costs to migrate away when you stop using it.
def: The cost of moving your data and workflow elsewhere when you abandon a given approach.
退出成本.why: Two sides of the same coin as substitutability. Invisible at selection time, most painful when something breaks.

闭源模型.purpose: You do not get the weights; you can only call it through the official interface.
def: Models whose weights are not published, usable only through the provider's API or product.
闭源模型.why: Usually stronger and updated faster, but data leaves your machine, you pay per use, and you carry outage risk.

隐私与合规.purpose: Which machines data passes through, how long it is retained, and whether it is audited.
def: Constraints around personal information, commercial secrets and industry regulation.
隐私与合规.why: This is a **veto item** in selection rather than a bonus — a non-compliant option cannot be used however good it is.

_strength: 选型层的措辞保留原文强度：「否决项」→ veto item、「硬约束」→ hard constraint，不软化。

AI Agent 与聊天机器人的区别.purpose: A chatbot's job ends with an answer; an agent's ends with the work being done.
def: A chatbot is question and answer. An agent plans its own steps, calls tools, checks results and loops until finished.
AI Agent 与聊天机器人的区别.why: Which of the two you are looking at decides whether it is worth your time to configure.

Token.purpose: The smallest unit a model processes text in. Both billing and length limits are measured in it.
def: The pieces a model splits text into. One token is roughly a quarter of an English word, or one to two Chinese characters.
Context length and API pricing are both denominated in tokens.
Token.why: The most easily overlooked word that most affects your bill. "Is my context enough" and "why is this so expensive" are both answered here.

开源生态.purpose: Models, tools, data and documentation all maintained by the community, freely combinable.
def: A collaborative system built on public code and community contribution, especially active around models and quantisations.
开源生态.why: When choosing local deployment, this ecosystem's activity directly determines how many ready-made solutions you can get.

成本.purpose: What an AI approach actually costs. Beyond unit price there is also how much you consume.
def: The real expense once costs are amortised across a task.
It comprises unit price times actual consumption (token count, duration, concurrency).
成本.why: **Choosing a model on unit price alone is easy to get wrong** — two models with identical prices can invert once real consumption differs.

生成式 AI.purpose: AI that produces new content from nothing — text, images, audio, video all count.
def: AI that samples from an existing data distribution to generate new content, as opposed to discriminative AI which only judges or classifies.
生成式 AI.why: Nearly all AI you encounter is generative. Its capability boundary differs sharply from recognition and classification.

能力边界.purpose: Knowing precisely what a model cannot do prevents more mistakes than knowing what it can.
def: The region outside the range in which a system reliably produces correct output for a given input.
能力边界.why: It is core literacy for using AI — keep important tasks inside the reliable range.

词表.purpose: The full set of characters a model knows. Its size decides whether it handles Chinese or code well.
def: The set of characters or pieces a model can use when producing output.
The larger the vocabulary, the more concepts the model must learn, and usually the better support for rare languages and code.
词表.why: It explains a common observation: small models get markedly worse at Chinese and code — there simply are not enough pieces in the vocabulary.

系统提示.purpose: The role and rules set for a model, which determine the tone of the whole conversation.
def: Instructions preset by the application developer, outside the user's input, constraining behaviour and output format.
系统提示.why: It is why the same model behaves so differently across applications. Every AI product you use has one behind it.

自动驾驶.purpose: The vehicle senses its surroundings, plans a route and controls the steering itself.
def: A technology system for autonomous driving using sensor fusion and AI decision-making.
自动驾驶.why: The most mature application of embodied AI, and the one with clear established grading levels.

视频生成.purpose: Generating short video clips from text or images.
def: Producing video content conditioned on a text prompt or a still image.
视频生成.why: It is the next step beyond image generation, and the gap between a striking demo and controllable output is still wide.

权限.purpose: The set of operations a tool is allowed to perform. Wider is more convenient and more dangerous.
def: The permitted action scope of a tool. A wider scope is easier to use and easier to get into trouble with.
Good tools authorise in tiers: reading needs approval, writing needs approval, deleting needs confirmation.
权限.why: It is the first gate on AI tool safety. **Giving a tool that writes files and runs commands no permission limits is handing over the machine.**

沙箱.purpose: Confine what the AI does to a controlled environment so a mistake stays contained.
def: An isolated execution environment — a container or restricted directory — limiting which files and commands it can touch.
沙箱.why: When judging whether an agent tool is trustworthy, first check whether it runs sandboxed by default.

浏览 - 网页操作.purpose: Let the AI click pages, fill forms and take screenshots to gather information.
def: Technology controlling a browser programmatically, used by many agents to collect information.
浏览 - 网页操作.why: It is both one of the most useful capabilities and one of the most security-sensitive, because it can operate real accounts.

量化.purpose: Compress model weights from high to low precision, saving VRAM and speeding things up at the cost of quality.
def: Representing each weight value with fewer bits. The common unit is bpw — average bits per weight.
Fewer bits saves more but loses more quality.
量化.why: The core technique in local deployment. For the same model, choosing the right quantisation tier often decides whether it runs at all.

预填充.purpose: The step where your whole input is read through before generation begins.
def: The stage where the model processes the input portion. Longer input means slower prefill and higher time to first token.
预填充.why: It explains a common observation: after you paste a long document the model "thinks" for a long time before answering — that is prefill computing.

首字延迟.purpose: How long from sending a question to seeing the first word. This number decides whether it feels fast.
def: The time taken to produce the first token, driven mainly by prompt length and whether prefill is needed.
首字延迟.why: The key metric for perceived speed. A model that generates fast per token but waits three seconds for the first one still feels slow.

本地部署.purpose: Download the model and run it on your own machine, so data never leaves.
def: Running model inference on your own hardware or server, without going through a third-party API.
本地部署.why: Usually the better choice when data is sensitive, when you need a specific quantisation, or when calling at high volume long-term.

模型评测的局限.purpose: A leaderboard score is not the same as your actual result — this matters.
def: Public evaluations struggle to cover your specific task, and suffer from data contamination and staleness.
模型评测的局限.why: The right approach is a small-scale test with your own real tasks rather than reading leaderboards alone.

社区与文档.purpose: When something breaks, can you find someone to ask, and is the API properly documented.
def: Non-technical factors: project activity, documentation quality, responsiveness to issues.
社区与文档.why: It carries heavy weight in selection while being the easiest to overlook — poor documentation consumes your time for a long time.

缓存策略.purpose: Do not recompute repeated content; reuse it directly. The first lever for cutting cost.
def: Caching repeated inputs and results to avoid duplicate calls and computation.
缓存策略.why: Its effect on cost is often larger than choosing a cheaper model.

AI 产品 vs AI 模型.purpose: Separate the model itself from the piece of software you actually use.
def: The model is the underlying capability; the product wraps it with interface, billing, collaboration features and permission management.
One model can appear inside many products, and the experience varies widely.
AI 产品 vs AI 模型.why: It explains why "top of the model leaderboard" does not mean "the tool you use is the best".

def: Technology converting text into natural-sounding speech.
语音合成.why: It is the output side of any voice feature. It can now produce tone and emotion close to a real person.

语音识别.purpose: Turn what was said into text.
def: Technology converting an audio signal into text, also called speech-to-text.
语音识别.why: It is the entry point for all voice interaction, and transcription quality directly caps how well the rest of the system understands.

采样 - 采样参数.purpose: How the model picks among candidate tokens — this determines how far the output diverges.
def: A collective term for parameters controlling generation: temperature, Top-p, Top-k and so on.
They affect only how a token is chosen, not the intelligence of the model itself.
采样 - 采样参数.why: Once you know these parameters, unstable output has an explainable cause instead of "it was feeling odd today".
